questions.q: What is the correct, case-sensitive top-level structure of a DQDL document?
options: A YAML file with a 'rules:' key at the root
A list named Rules, delimited by square brackets, containing one or more comma-separated rules
A Python dictionary passed directly to a Glue job's arguments
A JSON object with a 'validations' array
questions.explain: DQDL's real syntax is `Rules = [ ... ]` — a capitalized, bracketed list of rules, which is case-sensitive.

questions.q: Which rule types already return a true/false result on their own, without needing a comparison expression?
options: Completeness and StandardDeviation
RowCount and Sum
ColumnValues and Mean
IsComplete and IsUnique
questions.explain: IsComplete and IsUnique are inherently Boolean. Rule types like ColumnValues, Mean, and Completeness return a value that needs an expression (>, <, between, etc.) to become pass/fail.

questions.q: By default, how does AWS Glue Data Quality evaluate a composite rule like (ColumnValues "myCol1" > 1) OR (ColumnValues "myCol2" > 2)?
options: It evaluates each individual rule independently across the entire column, then combines the two overall pass/fail results — not row by row
It only evaluates the first rule and ignores the second
It automatically fails if either rule has ever failed in any previous run
It checks both conditions against the same row and passes if either is true for that row
questions.explain: The default behavior evaluates each side of the OR across the whole dataset independently, then combines the overall results — genuinely different from row-by-row SQL-style OR logic.

questions.q: What setting must be explicitly configured to make a composite rule evaluate row by row instead of the column-wide default?
options: There is no way to change this behavior
Switching the rule from OR to AND
Adding the keyword ROWWISE directly inside the DQDL rule itself
compositeRuleEvaluation.method set to "ROW" in the job's additionalOptions
questions.explain: Setting compositeRuleEvaluation.method to "ROW" in additionalOptions is the documented way to switch composite rules to per-row evaluation.

questions.q: What is the real functional difference between running DQDL rules inside a Glue ETL job versus attaching them directly to a table in the Glue Data Catalog?
options: DynamicRules, Analyzers, and Labels are only supported inside a Glue ETL job, not in Catalog-attached Data Quality
There is no functional difference between the two options
Catalog-attached rules support more rule types than ETL job rules
Catalog-attached rules can only check row counts, nothing else
questions.explain: Catalog-attached Data Quality is simpler to set up but lacks DynamicRules, Analyzers, and Labels, which require running the rules inside an actual Glue ETL job.
